NEWS FROM THE BOARD NEWS FROM THE BOARD A monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners Welcome to the monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners. We are happy to share information on significant news and events in Ada County. April 2025 Ryan Davidson - Commissioner Rod Beck - Chairman Tom Dayley - Commissioner ADA COUNTY VICTIM SERVICES CENTER RECOGNIZES SEXUAL ASSAULT, CHILD ABUSE PREVENTION, AND CRIME VICTIMS’ WEEK April is a meaningful month as it marks the awareness for Sexual Assault, Child Abuse Prevention, and Crime Victims’ Week. On April 9, 2025, the Center had the privilege of hosting the Sexual Assault Awareness and Prevention Campaign in conjunction with our valued community partners. We were honored to have Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck proclaim April as Sexual Assault Awareness Month for Ada County. We were also presented with the State of Idaho’s Sexual Assault Awareness Proclamation signed by Governor Brad Little. Our presenters included Boise Police Chief Chris Dennison, Idaho State Police Forensic Laboratory Director Matthew Gammett, SANE Forensic Nurse Valerie Nicasio, and Terry Reilly Associate Behavioral Health Director Britney Journee, LCPC. Each spoke about the importance of having a holistic, trauma-focused approach with survivors of sexual assault. Sexual assault is a crime that affects the individual, their loved ones, and our community. Most importantly, we recognized the courage of those affected by sexual assault and their willingness to speak their truth. Trina Allen Director, Ada County Victim Services Center If you or someone you know has been a victim of Sexual Assault, we encourage you to reach out to the Center at 208-577-4400. Our doors are open 24/7. Please reach out if you have questions or concerns for a loved one.

5 COUNTY GOVERNMENT MONTH The Annual Proclamation highlights the importance of the essential services provided by all Idaho Counties for their residents Did you know that everyone in Idaho lives within a county? Did you also know that the services provided by county government in each of Idaho’s 44 counties are mandated by the state legislature? On April 1, 2025 the Ada County Board of Commissioners signed a proclamation designating April as County Government Month. Every year since 1991, the National Association of Counties (NACO) has encouraged local counties across the country to elevate awareness of all the services, programs and responsibilities carried out by our counties. In Ada County, our nine elected officials and 2000+ employees work each day to provide outstanding service to those who live, work, and visit our communities. Ada County performs a vast array of critically important services our community counts on including the Ada County Landfill, Ada County Emergency Management & Community Resilience, Ada County Weed, Pest and Mosquito Abatement, Juvenile Services, Ada County Development Services, Ada County Parks & Waterways Barber Park, Expo Idaho and the Western Idaho Fair, Ada County Elections, the Ada County Treatment Center and the Ada County Victim Services Center, to name just a few. Thank you to everyone who works hard every day to help our communities flourish. Pictured L-R: Ada County Commissioner Tom Dayley, Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck and Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson

6 ARE YOU NEW TO THE AREA? Learn what a Mosquito Abatement District is Test your knowledge! Do you know what a mosquito abatement district does? Have you seen or heard a fogging truck, or are you new to the area and curious about how Ada County protects residents from mosquito-borne diseases like West Nile Virus? Ada County is home to a full-scale mosquito management operation that blends science, data, and fieldwork to keep our communities safe. Check out this video to see what goes on behind the scenes at the Ada County Mosquito Abatement District (ACMAD). We’ll show you how our team tracks, tests, and treats mosquito populations across the county. You’ll learn: • Mosquito surveillance techniques • How larvicide and adulticide treatments work • How ACMAD detects West Nile virus in mosquitoes • Steps taken to protect public health during the mosquito season Learn more at: https://adacounty.id.gov/ weedpestmosquito/mosquito-abatement

7 APRIL 18, 2025 TWO LIGHTS FOR TOMORROW On July 4, 2026, Americans will celebrate and honor the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. This milestone embodies our nation’s founding ideals of equality, liberty, and justice for all. Ada County Commissioners signed a proclamation on April 15, 2025, designating April 18, 2025 as “Two Lights for Tomorrow Day.” As part of a national initiative, two lights were displayed at the courthouse to honor and draw inspiration from Paul Revere’s historic ride to unite Americans in reflection, celebration, and service. This initiative aims to foster civic engagement and inspire acts of service that will resonate throughout our communities as we prepare for America’s 250th birthday in 2026. Learn more at https://america250.idaho.gov/ Pictured Left-Right: Ada County Treasurer Elizabeth Mahn, Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck, Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson, and Ada County Commissioner Tom Dayley. BECKY ALCALA CELEBRATES 30 YEARS WITH ADA COUNTY On April 22, 2025, the Ada County Commissioners’ conference room was packed as the county celebrated Becky Alcala’s thirty years of service. If you’ve done business with Development Services at any point in the last thirty years, you’ve likely interacted with Becky. Becky started her career with Ada County as a receptionist in Development Services on April 5th, 1995. About a year later, she was promoted to a Building Permit Specialist position where she spent 12 years assisting Ada County grow, one permit at a time. Becky was promoted to Planning and Building Specialist in 2012 and led the realignment and combination of application acceptance and building permit duties in Development Services. To recognize her leadership and the essential role of employees in Development Services handling permits and applications, Becky became the first-ever Permitting Division Supervisor in 2017. Her time as a supervisor was brief, however, as she was promoted to her current role as Office Administrator just a year later. It is routine for long-time contractors to ask Development Services Staff about Becky, as they miss her and hope to tell her hello. Some even ask about her family, as their children grew up and played sports with Becky’s boys. Becky currently takes care of Development Services in her role as Office Administrator at work and takes care of her husband, mom and mother-in-law at home. Family is her priority, and she is the center of the Development Services work family. Employees love to hear her laugh from her office area as she fills the office with love and laughter. She is a wealth of knowledge, the face behind the scenes making sure our operations run smoothly, and a friend and confidant to so many who walk through our doors. Thank you for 30 amazing years of service, Becky!!

8 We love it when children visit the Ada County Landfill and learn about trash. It’s so important to learn when you’re young – that when you throw something away it doesn’t just disappear. These images are from a recent tour given to preschoolers at the Learning Tree. This was the Monkey Class. We hope you are following the Ada County Landfill on Facebook. You’ll see more excruciatingly cute pictures like this. COMING IN MAY May is shaping up to be an action-packed month in Ada County. We look forward to sharing with you a ribbon-cutting event at the Ada County Landfill’s Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) facility. We’ll explain how this state-of-the-art facility will generate additional revenue for the county, which will offset future disposal fees for landfill users. Also on tap in next month’s newsletter – One of Ada County’s most beloved and respected department heads is retiring. We’ll have a profile. On May 22, 2025, Ada County’s Planning and Zoning Staff will continue hearing testimony on the County’s Zoning Ordinance Update. Follow Ada County Development Services on Facebook to keep informed on what’s planned and what happens next. Development Services Facebook And finally, we’ll share special recognition for Ada County Public Information Officers, Community Outreach, Training, and Education Staff. If you know about something happening in the county – it’s very likely that helpful information came from these folks! Thank you for reading the Ada County Newsletter. Remember to sign up to receive the newsletter automatically every month.
